title: Assessment of the noise impact of small aircraft with electrified distributed propulsion systems on humans - sub-study of the VIRLWINT project (Virtual Acoustic Twin of Distributed Propulsion Systems)
summary:
Research and development in the field of aviation is constantly endeavouring to make aircraft more efficient and faster, more climate-friendly and quieter. This applies to both large passenger transport and individual transport with small aircraft. Accordingly, new propulsion concepts and aircraft configurations are constantly being developed and tested. One example is electrified, distributed propulsion systems, which will initially be used for small aircraft with a capacity of 2 to 5 passengers (also known as air taxis). However, due to the large number of different configurations and the enormous costs involved, it would not be possible to first build and test every air taxi and then analyse its noise impact on the population in the vicinity of existing airports. For this reason, the aim is to use calculations and measurements in the wind tunnel at a very early stage of development to evaluate artificially audible aircraft noises - so-called auralisations - by test subjects. The aim of this study is to gain an impression of how people perceive and judge the sounds of future air taxis.
In addition to the usual listening tests in the laboratory, the aim is to develop a smartphone app to reach large numbers of test subjects outside the laboratory and incorporate their assessment of the aircraft sounds.
The results of this study should help to support the development of new air taxi concepts, identify particularly unpleasant sounding configurations and revise these or further improve configurations that are already less unpleasant and annoying. Furthermore, the results of this and other studies can serve as a basis for international regulatory bodies to derive noise certification and noise protection regulations.

interventions.name:
Sub-study 1: Focused listening test in the laboratory
The test subjects are presented with 80 different sounds lasting 15 seconds via a computer with closed headphones in ME's sound laboratory. All sounds are auralized, i.e. not recorded in real life, but made artificially audible using measurement

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Availability of the signed declarations of consent for data protection (for subject selection and for conducting the study), the subject contract and the subject consent form
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
- age-appropriate normal hearing in the frequency range 125 - 8000 Hz
Exclusion criteria:
- Hearing loss in the audiogram: i.e. the hearing thresholds in the better ear are higher than the 10th percentile of the gender- and age-specific hearing thresholds in ISO 7029 (2017)
- Wearing a hearing aid
- Hearing disorders (tinnitus with severity > 2, sudden hearing loss within the last 10 years)
- any other condition which, in the opinion of the doctors conducting the test, makes the subject unsuitable
- any medication with an influence on the test parameters or consumption of stimulants and drugs with an influence on the test parameters, e.g. drug consumption, increased alcohol consumption and nicotine consumption that does not allow abstinence for at least 10 hours
- persons without legal capacity and persons with limited legal capacity
- do not speak German
